A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Visual-TCAV work, and their supplied pages are readable. However, v2 references supplementary material that is absent from its PDF, limiting comparison of earlier additional examples and generation details with v3's included appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original local and global explanations, controlled synthetic-tag experiments, and comparisons with TCAV in Section 4.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and supplies additional explanation-evaluation results, stability studies, component ablations, and feature-map intervention experiments in Appendices F–K.

M1.justification: The difference-of-means CAV, spatial pooling, concept maps, and feature-space IG pipeline remain. As written, Section 3.3 revises attribution scaling from min-max normalization of logit differences to ReLU followed by division by the maximum positive difference (v3 Equations 4–5). The PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed accordingly.

E1.justification: ImageNet, CelebA, DTD, generated concepts, and the synthetic-tag classification task remain. Appendix F adds a task where GPT-5 judges which concept an explanation communicates as more important, while Appendix G tests concept examples contaminated with unrelated images. Coverage expands within the existing domains.

E2.justification: The external comparator methods remain TCAV, IG, and Grad-CAM; IG and Grad-CAM were already evaluated in v2. Appendix H adds explicitly evaluated normalization comparators: per-image min-max and spatial Max/Mean alternatives against the default Chmean normalization.

E3.justification: v3 supplies substantial additional evaluation protocols: GPT-5 judgments of 360 explanations, localization against known tag masks, alternative IG baselines and step counts, and interventions across 49 concept-class pairs. The retained main experiments keep their model families, tag percentages, and 300-step IG setting.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's controlled tag validation, v3 supplies studies of concept-example count and contamination (G), normalization choices (H), IG baselines (I), integration steps and runtime (J), and concept insertion/deletion faithfulness on larger networks (K). These examine previously unsupported robustness and component-design questions in the supplied material.

E5.justification: v2 already displays attribution error bars and TCAV significance markings. v3 adds 50 random sampling runs for the stability study and paired McNemar tests, alongside ablation summaries with ± values. Figure 7 also changes the stated nonsignificance inequality from p > 0.05 to p < 0.05, an apparent reporting error; increased repetition of retained experiments is not established.

E6.justification: New results include GPT-5 explanation-judgment accuracies of 98.33% for Visual-TCAV, 71.67% for Grad-CAM, and 65.83% for IG (Table 1), plus ablation, runtime, and intervention results (Tables 3–8). Figure 7 exposes previously suppressed nonsignificant scores while retaining displayed significant scores. The five untagged-test accuracies in v2 Section 4.4.1 are omitted.

T1.justification: Appendix K introduces formal definitions of the concept-aligned component, insertion/deletion paths, and their AUCs (Equations 7–10), including the reverse-path equivalence. Most additional equations in Section 3 formalize previously described computations; the existing IG completeness argument is retained without a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain concept localization, per-instance concept attribution, and aggregation into global explanations. The claim of better importance assessment than TCAV already appears in v2. v3's named desiderata and stronger supporting evidence do not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive qualifications about subjective concept selection, non-exhaustiveness of concept sets, and unreliable spatial grounding when adapting to ViTs. The appendices interpret normalization tradeoffs, baseline sensitivity, computational savings, and the limited generality of advice on example counts. Section 4.4.1 also distinguishes absent TCAV sensitivity from negative sensitivity.

D1.justification: v3 supplies exact GPT-5 evaluator prompts, Stable Diffusion v1.5 prompting and manual-filtering details, constructions for alternative IG baselines and interventions, and detailed runtime measurements. It newly specifies random tags on entity-negative examples. The hardware, software versions, main IG step count, and code URL were already disclosed in v2.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion of sparse autoencoders and mechanistic interpretability, acknowledges equivalence to Pahde et al. (2025), and adds references concerning synthetic CAVs and ViT spatial grounding. Several IG-variant citations disappear. The central positioning between saliency methods and user-defined concept explanations remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and limitations receive substantial editing. Section 3.3 is extensively reorganized into explained computational stages, and the contributions become named desiderata. Structured appendix navigation is added, although the main section order remains.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. Figures 6–7 are rebuilt as class-wise line plots, Figure 6 adds 50%-tag concept maps, and Figure 2 adds a chequered example. The included appendices add numerous visual comparisons, diagnostic plots, and eight tables.

improvement.justification: The supplied v2 chiefly validates faithfulness through a small controlled tag experiment. v3 substantially strengthens that evidence with component ablations and interventions across 49 concept-class pairs on larger networks, while improving technical documentation and applicability qualifications. The GPT-5 study establishes automated judgment performance rather than human usefulness, and Figure 7 introduces an erroneous significance inequality. These limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in validation and auditability.
